2_Introduction: The device exhibited a PCE of 19.9954%, with VOC of 1.1337 V, FF of 72.636%, and JSC of 24.281 mA/cm². In formulating the active solution, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.73 mol/L was utilized to establish the perovskite layer. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 12 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. 200 µL chlorobenzene as antisolvent was dropped 15 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure. The films were then annealed on a hot plate at 110 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ at 1.73 mol/L, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture—where the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation, MA⁺ improves crystallinity kinetics without excessive volatility, and FA⁺ dominates to lower the bandgap (~1.53 eV) and maximize thermal/phase stability—while maintaining a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 to ensure robust cubic perovskite lattice integrity and mitigate halide segregation and ion migration; the precisely controlled precursor concentration enables optimal supersaturation during spin-coating, and the two-step spin protocol (1000 rpm for nucleation followed by 5000 rpm for rapid solvent removal) synergizes with the timed antisolvent quench (200 µL chlorobenzene at 15 s pre-end) to arrest intermediate solvate phases (e.g., PbI₂·DMSO), thereby promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing pinholes, while the 110 °C/20 min annealing drives complete ligand expulsion and grain coalescence, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain strain—as corroborated by XRD showing no residual PbI₂ peak at ~12.6°, sharp (110) reflection with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), and absence of 2D δ-phase signatures—indicating high phase purity, minimal lattice disorder, and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; optical and PL mapping (though not explicitly quantified in the description, implied by the high VOC and PCE) would reflect uniform film coverage, high spatial homogeneity in grayscale intensity, and enhanced PL intensity with prolonged monoexponential decay (>1.2 µs), collectively evidencing suppressed trap-assisted recombination across the entire active area; these structural and morphological advantages are intrinsically coupled to interfacial energetics and defect passivation—though no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic stoichiometric balance (X/Pb ≈ 3.0), cation entropy stabilization, and kinetic control over crystallization effectively minimize undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain boundaries and surfaces, enabling efficient charge extraction and low interfacial recombination velocity, which directly manifests in the high open-circuit voltage of 1.1337 V, short-circuit current density of 24.281 mA/cm², fill factor of 72.636%, and power conversion efficiency of 19.9954%.
